rows.what the ink shows: A small open e-like hook is followed by a tall l-like upright and a long, nearly flat connector ending in a dark wedge. At fivefold enlargement the internal letter bodies, accents and separate abbreviation point are not individually resolved; the compressed continuation does not securely establish the complete proposed abbreviation.

The left curved arm joins a long vertical descender, while the upper-right stroke forms a closed oval with a small light counter. It has no separate upright central prong above the bowl. This is the looped varphi form also visible as the second sign of the unmarked psi-varphi pair lower on this page.

The left hooked arm meets a downward-curving stem; its right lobe is an enclosed, ink-filled oval. The stem does not rise independently between open arms as it does in the page's psi signs. This second occurrence therefore reads varphi.

A leading round bowl joins a tall slanting stroke, followed by another loop, a further upright and a small terminal curl. There is no clear j descender or pair of accents to establish deja. The close joins do not securely distinguish an a-l-o-r-s sequence from a d-e/l-a segmentation; the apparent word spacing and the accent needed by de là are not clear.

The glyph has a curled left arm, a short curved descender and an elongated closed right oval with a visible light center. That enclosed right lobe is the same varphi construction seen in the other two marked occurrences, rather than the independently rising central stroke of the page's psi.

On deliberate reinspection, the first group preserves only a low nub and a short rising stroke above the cancellation. The nub has no surviving e counter, and a separate t crossbar cannot be distinguished from the deletion line, so et remains uncertain. The later tall l-like stroke and its separate short rightward e-like bar survive clearly enough to read le.

The first-line est region is crossed by a heavy horizontal deletion and descending insertion strokes; its low bumps do not preserve distinct e-s-t joins. The following tall l and adjacent small rounded a-like body support la. In the next-line continuation, an opening upright/loop, elevated dots or accent marks, and two descending strokes remain consistent with réciproque, but several low connecting bodies are completely merged into the deletion. Those landmarks do not independently recover every letter of the proposed word, so réciproque remains uncertain after reconciliation.

The cancelled insertion preserves an initial short oblique crossing, then a small dark oval and taller loop farther right. A thick horizontal stroke merges with the original baseline across the entire span, so the surviving features do not independently establish e followed by t.

The opening Il is a tall crossed pair; a short n-like horizontal stroke is followed by a raised apostrophe and a y with a long curved descender. A separate small a-like spot precedes plus, whose descending p, tall l and low connected u-s strokes remain visible.

A tall initial stem and low left bowl-like remnant survive, together with a detached curved stroke above the right half. The horizontal cancellation fills the intervening letter bodies and the baseline. Even at fivefold enlargement it does not securely reveal an apostrophe and où, or a complete alternative alors sequence.

patterns.name: Closed right oval in varphi, separate central prong in psi
patterns.description: Each of these three marks has an enclosed right oval, sometimes filled by the pen, attached to a descending stem. The same-page unmarked psi-varphi pair and Donc psi show that psi instead has a distinct central rising prong between open arms. The three marked looped signs therefore independently support varphi.

patterns.name: Horizontal cancellation hides low letter bodies
patterns.description: These deletions repeatedly merge with the baseline. Taller strokes, dots and descenders survive while low letter joins disappear. M0060 preserves the later l/e group, and M0061 preserves a first-line l/a group plus dots and two descenders in the continuation, but those remaining landmarks do not establish all the surrounding cancelled letters.

metadata.notes: All ten IDs were personally inspected in the actual 1725 x 2222 source image and in the listed crops. No OCR, recognition tools or text layers were used. Hua was read only after initial visual inspection, as fallible comparison. Independent eyes were requested for the three Greek signs, M0058 and the cancelled M0060–M0062; the Greek readings agree, and M0058 retains segmentation uncertainty rather than being selected from grammar. M0055 and M0064 remain uncertain after enlargement. No secure unmarked correction was identified. This submission does not commit edits or authorize a later page. Targeted reconciliation: the same M0060_focus, M0061_start and M0061_tail_focus crops were personally re-inspected once against the independent reader's cautious proposals. The first et lacks a separately visible e counter or t crossbar; the proposed réciproque has useful landmarks but insufficient surviving low bodies. M0060 is therefore revised to \unsure{et} le, and M0061 to \unsure{est} la \unsure{réciproque}. M0058 retains alors|de là because no clear j descender is visible; the independent reader retained a broader set, and no grammatical choice was used.
